title: SYSK Selects: How Exorcism Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the episode on how exorcism works, introduced by Chuck. The hosts open with Philip K. Dick's claim that he was possessed by an alien intelligence that reordered his life, then contrast spirit possession beliefs worldwide with Western psychology. They cover psychological explanations for possession symptoms (epilepsy, schizophrenia, dissociative identity disorder) and treatments such as electroconvulsive therapy. They describe Catholic Church teaching on demonic possession and signs (speaking in foreign or unknown tongues, knowing hidden things, superhuman strength, aversion to sacred objects), the Rite of Exorcism (prayers, holy water, crucifixes, relics), the church's investigation process with psychological evaluation, and the rate of about one in five thousand cases deemed real. They discuss a sociologist's book on American exorcisms, the ten appointed priests and the International Association of Exorcists, and for-profit exorcism ministries led by Bob Larson, including a Toledo testimonial. A correction segment fixes a Framingham Heart Study misnomer ("Farmington").

segments.title: Selects intro and opening banter
segments.summary: Chuck introduces this Selects pick of the exorcism episode, noting its timing near Halloween. The hosts begin the show with the opening banter.

segments.title: Philip K. Dick and alleged possession
segments.summary: The hosts describe science fiction writer Philip K. Dick, who believed an alien intelligence possessed him and reorganized his life. He held that belief until he died.

segments.title: Spirit possession worldwide vs. Western view
segments.summary: The hosts note that Western society in the twenty-first century mostly does not believe in spirit intrusion, while many parts of the world commonly do. They ask whether psychological disorders are sometimes misread as possession.

segments.title: Psychological explanations and treatments
segments.summary: Possession may be mistaken for epilepsy, schizophrenia, or dissociative identity disorder. Psychological treatments include antidepressants, psychotherapy, and electroconvulsive therapy.

segments.title: Catholic Church, possession signs, and The Exorcist
segments.summary: The Catholic Church still practices exorcism and believes in demonic possession. Signs include speaking in unlearned languages, knowing hidden things, superhuman strength, and aversion to sacred objects. The hosts compare these with the film The Exorcist, with Linda Blair.

segments.title: The Rite of Exorcism and church investigation
segments.summary: The rite combines prayers with call and response, holy water, crucifixes, and relics. Before an exorcism, the church investigates with a psychological evaluation. The hosts say about one in five thousand cases is judged a real possession or worth exorcising.

segments.title: Sociologist's study, exorcist priests, and for-profit exorcisms
segments.summary: A sociologist's book on American exorcisms describes a man named Warren who felt better afterward. The church has appointed about eleven exorcists, who belong to the International Association of Exorcists. Bob Larson's ministry holds ticketed exorcisms, and a Toledo woman's testimonial is discussed.

segments.title: Correction time: Framingham Heart Study
segments.summary: A listener corrects Chuck's mispronunciation of the Framingham Heart Study as the Farmington study. The hosts close with a call for listener email.
